{"chapter_reviews":[{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"Mostly separated: the Hadhoud, Sinai, mass-trial, refugee, and LGBT records identify allegations, uncertainty, or official contrary accounts; C1-007 and C1-008 particularly distinguish defense allegations from judicial and prosecution dispositions. However, broad composite claims in WD002 and WD010 should be split into individually attributable claim units, and the police-pardon beneficiary link remains reported rather than officially verified.","closed_system_silence":"High risk. Prison access, Sinai reporting, independent monitoring, and official-file access were restricted; lack of public complaints, verified casualty totals, or published discipline cannot be treated as evidence of safety or accountability.","duplicate_reporting":"Material concentration exists. WD015 and WEB-3B-C1-001 duplicate the same official speech and should be one stable fact with corroboration; WEB-3B-C1-002 is corroborative coverage of that same speech. WD008 and WEB-3B-C1-003 concern the same execution videos, while WD005 and WEB-3B-C1-006 both depend on the unverified beneficiary-document account. Repeated coverage must not be treated as independent confirmation of the underlying incidents.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both were performed. The notebook preserves releases/pardons, the human-rights strategy, FGM enforcement, individual minority-protection actions, the prosecution's Hadhoud account, and reduced reported insurgent activity alongside adverse material. Further targeted work is still warranted where favorable official remedy claims lack underlying records.","missing_source_type":"Primary or authenticated official records are missing for the pardon beneficiaries, full Hadhoud forensic/investigative file, prison complaints/visits, and any military or prosecutorial investigation into Sinai executions. Independent Arabic local reporting and remedy records are also needed for vulnerable-group protection.","official_claim_independence":"Official claims are not accepted uncritically: C1-008 is paired with independent objections and C1-005 expressly does not identify beneficiaries. Nonetheless, the most consequential official links—pardon beneficiaries, forensic findings, and absence of military investigation—lack independently inspectable primary files.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Documented detention and abuse counts are case-based and may be incomplete, while advocacy and media reporting can cluster around visible incidents. They establish documented patterns and events, not national prevalence; the notebook generally states this limitation.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Authority, inherited repression, the Sinai insurgency, and reporting constraints are explicitly addressed. Population exposure is only partly resolved: national reporting is not disaggregated enough by geography or affected population, and the end-of-year safety assessment lacks recovered country-year physical-integrity trend data.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WD001","WD002","WD003","WD004","WD005","WD006","WD008","WD009","WD010","WD011","WD012","WD013","WD014","WD015","WEB-3B-C1-001","WEB-3B-C1-003","WEB-3B-C1-005","WEB-3B-C1-006","WEB-3B-C1-007","WEB-3B-C1-008","WEB-3B-C1-009","WEB-3B-C1-011","WEB-3B-C1-012"],"unresolved_risks":["Security-force and militia conduct is attributable on an authority-based national-responsibility basis, but there is no evidence of Sisi's personal order, knowledge, or approval for the Sinai executions.","The reported identification of pardoned convicted officers remains dependent on leaked-document reporting; Decree 13/2022 proves the mechanism, not the beneficiaries.","Restricted access makes both abuse prevalence and the claimed effectiveness of oversight/remedies difficult to establish.","The 2021–2022 end-state comparison has partial measures but lacks recovered structured physical-integrity series and sufficiently broad population/geographic coverage."]},"chapter_id":"3B","defensible_evidence_estimate":22,"independent_source_family_estimate":10,"missing_themes":["3B.2 — Official command, oversight, or investigation material concerning army-aligned Sinai forces is missing; a bounded archival and local-source search could test operational responsibility without requiring a personal-order theory.","3B.3 — The recovered May speech supports hostile collective labeling but not incitement. A bounded 2022 presidential-speech archive search could determine whether other direct rhetoric materially changes that narrow finding.","3B.4 — The official pardon beneficiary annex, Hadhoud autopsy/investigation materials, and usable prison-complaint or visit records remain unavailable; these are material to remedy and accountability.","3B.5 — The asserted 2022 successor emergency-power framework lacks a developed, precise source-claim record for the relevant statute, powers, and application; recoverable legal-text evidence is needed.","3B.7 — Vulnerable-group coverage is broad but remedy evidence remains uneven and concentrated in U.S. reporting and advocacy sources; bounded Arabic local and case-record work could test actual protection and remedies.","3B.9 — Crisis-response evidence does not yet resolve the state response to the Sinai execution material or independently test investigation/discipline; targeted official and local records could improve this.","3B.10 — The end-of-period comparison needs recoverable 2021–2022 physical-integrity indicator rows and more population/geographic-specific safety evidence; the current death-penalty and terrorism series are informative but incomplete."],"substantive_issues":["The notebook recreates the same speech fact under WD015 and WEB-3B-C1-001; consolidate it under one stable global evidence ID and attach WEB-3B-C1-002 as corroboration. Reconcile the same-video execution coverage similarly.","WD002 and WD010 bundle materially distinct source-supported claims. Split them into discrete evidence units before downstream use so that each claim, locator, attribution basis, and contrary account can be assessed separately.","The direct presidential-pardon claim is defensible only as a class-based pardon mechanism plus a separately qualified report of beneficiaries; do not present the beneficiary link as verified official fact until a named annex or case record is recovered.","The notebook fairly records shared operational authority and target-period uncertainty for the Sinai killings, but should not allow repeated video coverage to imply an established presidential command chain.","Several asserted contextual legal and inherited-baseline propositions are not represented by a corresponding developed machine record. They may orient interpretation, but should not substitute for cited evidence on the selected lenses."]}],"global_findings":["The selected chapter has substantial adverse and contrary material across the ten lenses, but material recoverable gaps remain in official remedy evidence, successor emergency-law documentation, Sinai accountability, vulnerable-group remedies, and end-period comparison.","No scores, score ranges, rankings, or judge-directed recommendations were found.","The local-data audit was used as a contextual prior only; no underlying country-year values were supplied, so it is not counted as developed evidence.","Continuation should be bounded to the listed 3B lenses and source types; duplicate consolidation and claim splitting are deterministic cleanup, not new research."],"needs_continuation":true,"reviewer_summary":"3B is not ready for a no-continuation handoff. Its central governing-conduct picture is supported, and contrary evidence is materially preserved, but targeted research can still improve attribution, legal precision, independent remedy testing, and the 2021–2022 safety comparison.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":["3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10"]}
